title: Burst allocator: client-facing rate-signal, temporary credit caps, and invoice protection
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Customers on Dedicated pools are occasionally receiving short-duration surge capacity (temporary boosts) from the burst allocator when autoscaling cannot provision capacity quickly enough. These temporary boosts reduce request latency but create two issues: 1) invoice surprises when overage charges materialize with no clear customer-visible accounting, and 2) noisy rate signals where clients can't distinguish normal throttling from temporary-credit drains.

Goal: Define a spec and implementation plan for a burst allocation policy that: (a) exposes a clear rate-signal and remaining-burst-credit counter to customers via the Console + API; (b) enforces soft caps and graceful throttles when temporary boost budget is nearly depleted; (c) amortizes overage billing in a customer-friendly way (billing smoothing and invoice annotations); (d) provides operator controls to drain or revoke surge pools for a tenant.

Key proposal details:
- Terminology: "surge credit" = ephemeral capacity tokens consumed when autoscaler falls behind. "Burst window" = 15s default window for allocation.
- Client-facing telemetry: add fields to the dedicated status endpoint and token-level traces: surge_credit_remaining (ms equivalence), surge_window_start, last_boost_reason (autoscaler|pool-drain|manual). Console will show per-route countdown and recent boost events.
- Soft caps & graceful throttles: when surge_credit_remaining <= 20% we switch to a token-leaky fallback: accept requests up to 70% of prior throughput and return header X-Redwood-Burst-State:almost-depleted. After credit exhaustion, fall back to configured policy (throttle|fallback-model|queue).
- Billing & invoice behavior: annotate usage with a separate line-item for "surge-boosted tokens". Implement invoice smoothing where ephemeral boosts for the last billing cycle are amortized and flagged with reason/event IDs; enable an "invoice-protection" flag for high-confidence customers which will offset first X minutes of boost against reserved capacity (operator configurable).
- Operator controls: add an admin endpoint to place a tenant's surge pool in pause/force-drain modes, and a CLI action to reject further temporary boosts for a window. Audit logs and alerts must record operator-driven revocations.
- Backwards compatibility: default client telemetry fields should be opt-out; existing API contracts preserve previous shapes.

Success criteria:
- Console accuracy: 95% of observed boost events map to a console entry within 30s (based on synthetic smoke test dashboards).
- Invoice clarity: >90% of surveyed pilot customers report invoice clarity (pilot N=8) and no unexpected overages for test scenarios.
- Runtime safety: rollout must not increase tail latency for non-boosted requests beyond 3% p95.

Rollout plan:
1) Spec review and API contract (this ticket) -> 1 week.
2) Telemetry + Console mockups -> design + PM signoff (2 weeks).
3) Runtime change: surge_credit book-keeping + soft-cap leak policy behind feature flag (3 weeks).
4) Billing pipeline: usage annotation + invoice smoothing prototype in staging (2 weeks).
5) Pilot with 3 low-risk customers (4 weeks).

Telemetry & dashboards:
- New chart: surge_credits_consumed_per_tenant (per-minute), surge_boost_events (labelled by reason), surge_exhaustion_count.
- Alerts: surge_exhaustion_rate > 0.5% of requests for 5m -> ops paging.

API/Console changes (high level):
- GET /v1/dedicated/{tenant}/status adds surge_credit_remaining, last_boost_id, last_boost_reason.
- Console: tenant capacity view adds "Burst credit" bar with hover tooltip linking to recent boost events and billing note.

Dependencies and open work:
- Billing ingestion changes (depends on ENG-50901) for line-item annotation.
- Operator drain controls require small RBAC extension (eng: infra-auth).
- Design mockups to be provided by DES-1284 (design task).

Open questions:
- Default surge window duration: 15s vs 60s tradeoff (short windows reduce billing surprise but increase churn).
- Whether invoice smoothing should be automatic or opt-in for customers with reserved capacity.
- How to surface historical boost usage in CSV exports for finance teams.
